section_title: What changes when the Lord’s glory returns?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Then the man brought me back to the gate that faces east, 2 and I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of many waters, and the earth shone with His glory. 3 The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when He came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the River Kebar. I fell facedown, 4 and the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east. 5 Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

context_lines: The measured temple is now filled with the presence for which it was prepared. Ezekiel is brought to the east gate and sees the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice is like the roar of many waters, and His glory lights the earth.

Ezekiel recognizes the appearance from his earlier visions by the River Kebar and of the city’s destruction. He falls facedown. The Spirit then lifts him into the inner court, and he sees the glory filling the temple.
This reverses the movement in chapters 10–11, when the glory departed toward the east. The promise is more than the restoration of a building: the Lord returns to dwell among His people.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/43.htm) emphasizes the reversal of the departure: the glory that went eastward now returns from the east. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/43.htm) sees the vision of God’s glory as leading readers toward the gifts of God through Christ.
The return is the turning point of the temple vision. Measurements and arrangements give way to the Lord’s presence.
god_plan_lines: A close parallel appears in [Revelation 1:12–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/revelation/1.htm). The risen Jesus has a voice like many waters, His face shines like the sun, and John falls at His feet. Jesus identifies Himself as the One who died and is alive forever, and reassures John.

[Matthew 17:1–8](https://biblehub.com/bsb/matthew/17.htm) also shows Jesus shining with glory, the disciples falling facedown and Jesus telling them not to fear. These accounts connect the awe of God’s revealed glory with the glory of Christ. The New Testament adds the assurance that this glorious Lord is the Savior who has overcome death and draws near to His people.
